meeting_header:
Date: 2027-02-25
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Redwood: Liam O'Keefe (AE), Priya Ramesh (SE), Marcus Hale (SE)
Customer: Jonathan Pike (Head of Security), Aisha Khan (IT Ops), Renee Lopez (Compliance)
summary: Redwood walked through SOC 2/ISO27001 posture items, demonstrated Trust Center access patterns, discussed KMS options and audit log exports. Customer requested redacted SOC 2 Type II report and control mapping template; wants clarity on Key Management options (AWS KMS vs on-prem HSM) and RBAC roles for Trust Center access. Agreed to schedule KMS integration walkthrough and share artifacts.
topics: SOC 2 Type II artifacts and redaction rules
Audit logs: retention, export, and residency
transcript:
[00:00] Liam (AE): Hi all, thanks for joining uh we're on for 60 minutes today, we'll run through your SOC2/ISO posture and the trust center path, and Priya will cover the KMS bits.
[00:14] Jonathan (Nova): Great thanks Liam, yeah we, we wanted a clear picture of what access you'll need and what artifacts you can provide, um and how keys are handled especially for patient genomic data.
[00:29] Priya (SE): Yep, absolutely. Quick agenda: trust center access, what redacted reports we can share, control mapping, then KMS options and audit log exports. Sound ok?
[00:41] Renee (Nova): Sounds good. Also we have our internal auditors on a tight timeline - ISO gap review next month.
[00:49] Marcus (SE): Noted. We'll flag items that typically come up in audits. A quick note: our Trust Center supports scoped viewer roles so you don't need full admin to see evidence.
[01:05] Aisha (Nova): When you say trust center, is that a portal or a doc repo? We saw a link in the deck but need to know who to invite and least-privilege roles.
[01:18] Liam (AE): It's a portal - web UI with per-route and per-report RBAC. We'll send a temporary viewer role so your compliance team can browse redacted artifacts. Priya will outline recommended roles.
[01:33] Priya (SE): For SOC 2 Type II we can provide a redacted full report and a control-by-control mapping. Redaction usually strips customer identifiable examples but keeps control descriptions, testing period, and evidence pointers.
[01:49] Jonathan: Ok, redaction is fine, but we need signed attestation or something auditors will accept. Do you provide the auditor letter or only internal artifacts?
[01:58] Priya: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and the auditor's opinion letter; both are accessible via Trust Center under the "Reports" section. The thing to call out is, any customer-specific PII will be redacted per the redaction template.
[02:14] Jonathan: Right. And KMS - we have a requirement to control keys for certain datasets. Do you support customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[02:24] Priya: Yes. Two modes: hosted keys (Redwood-managed keys in our KMS) and customer-managed keys. For customer-managed we support AWS KMS CMKs and we also have an HSM gateway integration for on-prem HSMs, though that path requires a short engineering onboarding window.
[02:42] Aisha: If we use AWS KMS, does Redwood have any ability to decrypt without our keys? We need to ensure you cannot decrypt outside audit windows.
[02:53] Marcus: Short answer: no. With customer-managed CMKs the service encrypts at rest with keys that you control; Redwood cannot extract plaintext without key usage being permitted. There are audit logs around decrypt operations.
[03:07] Jonathan: And rotation? Policy wise we need rotation every 90 days for the sensitive env.
[03:12] Priya: That is supported — we recommend automated rotation in the KMS policy. If you have HSM you'll manage rotation on-prem; we can surface rotation events in the Trust Center.
[03:25] Renee: Audit logs — what do they look like? Can we ingest them to our SIEM?
[03:33] Liam: Yes, we export structured audit logs (JSON) for important events: key usage, model calls, user logins, config changes. You can push to S3/CloudWatch or we can ship to your SIEM via webhook or syslog forwarder.
[03:50] Aisha: Retention? We need 7 years for certain controls.
[03:55] Priya: Default retention is 1 year in the hosted plan, but for Enterprise we support configurable retention policies up to multi-year; for 7 years we usually provision long-term cold storage in your account or an encrypted object store in our enterprise plan. We'll include retention options in the follow-up.
[04:16] Jonathan: Data residency — some datasets must never leave EU. How do you ensure region locking and that logs and model state are kept in-region?
[04:27] Marcus: We have region routing and private deployments. For strict residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated models provisioned in the EU region. Audit logs and backups can be configured to stay in the selected region.
[04:41] Aisha: Ok. Can you map controls to ISO27001 rather than just SOC? Our audit will look for ISO clauses.
[04:48] Priya: Yes, we create a combined mapping template that crosswalks SOC controls to ISO27001 Annex A clauses. We'll attach that mapping in the control mapping template.
[04:58] Jonathan: What about SSO and RBAC? We use SAML with Okta. Can we federate and limit Trust Center access by groups?
[05:07] Liam: Yes, SAML SSO via Okta is supported. You can map Okta groups to Trust Center roles so auditors can grant read-only to the compliance group and admin to a small ops subset.
[05:19] Renee: Are there known gaps auditors raise with the Redwood footprint? Anything to pre-warn our ISO team about?
[05:26] Marcus: Common asks: evidence around model updates and deployment rollouts, KV cache handling, and details of fallback policies. We'll include deployment runbooks and change logs in the Trust Center evidence.
[05:40] Jonathan: How do you show chain of custody for models and data during POCs? We sometimes need a signed handoff.
[05:48] Priya: For POCs we can provide a scope-limited evidence bundle plus a handoff doc. It's not a signed legal transfer but it's detailed enough for most auditors; if you need formal attestation we can topo into enterprise legal.
[06:05] Aisha: Quick nit: in your docs I saw references to "KV cache" — our security team wants to understand whether that persists across requests or is ephemeral.
[06:14] Marcus: The KV cache is per-session for the runtime and can be configured to not persist beyond the session; in Dedicated/Private you can control cache persistence and we document default TTLs in the evidence.
[06:28] [crosstalk] Jonathan: (laughs) good.
[06:31] Liam: Ok, shifting to specifics — Priya, could you walk through the artifacts we will upload and the sample redactions?
[06:38] Priya: Sure. Typical artifact set: SOC2 Type II report, auditor opinion letter, control testing workpapers (redacted), configuration screenshots, deployment runbooks, KMS policy snippets, and audit log samples. Redactions will remove PII and customer-specific identifiers but keep enough context for auditors.
[06:58] Renee: Will the auditor be able to contact Redwood directly if they need clarification?
[07:04] Priya: Yes we provide an auditor contact path — usually a designated security contact and a support ticket route; we can provide an NDA'd channel if desired.
[07:14] Jonathan: On the KMS HSM gateway, how long does onboarding take? We have maintenance windows and strict change controls.
[07:22] Marcus: For AWS KMS CMK mode it's quick — hours to a couple of days for validation. For on-prem HSM gateway, plan for 2-4 weeks for connectivity, network validation, and HSM policy integration. We'll document exact steps in the onboarding checklist.
[07:40] Aisha: About decrypt operations — you mentioned logs for decrypts. Can we require dual-approval for certain decrypts?
[07:48] Priya: That's more of a policy layer — if you use an on-prem HSM with a pre-approval workflow you can require manual approval. For AWS KMS, you can enforce IAM conditions and CloudTrail alerting; full dual-approval would need integration with your workflow tool but is doable.
[08:06] Jonathan: Are the Trust Center access logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence.
[08:12] Liam: We store logs with append-only pattern and sign ingestion events; for high-assurance customers we can ship logs to your S3 bucket in your account for immutability guarantees via object lock.
[08:26] Renee: Any limitations around exporting large log volumes for long retention? Our SIEM costs scale.
[08:33] Priya: We try to be efficient — exports are incremental. For multi-year retention we recommend storing compressed, encrypted archives in your account to control egress costs. We'll include an estimate for projected storage and egress in follow-up.
[08:50] Marcus: Also note, when you use Dedicated pools, audit sampling may be more granular and less noisy for your compliance team.
[08:59] Aisha: One more on residency: if we pick EU-only, do you still keep any metadata in US for control plane?
[09:06] Priya: The control plane for Redwood Private can be customer-hosted; for hosted plans some metadata about usage is stored in our control plane regions but we can provide a control plane VPC peering option or bring-your-own-control-plane for strict residency. We'll detail tradeoffs.
[09:21] Jonathan: Ok, that helps. Next, about evidence delivery — can you give our auditors a temporary live view during their window instead of delivering a big bundle?
[09:30] Liam: Yes, short lived viewer roles to the Trust Center are best practice. We can time them to your audit window and revoke after.
[09:39] Renee: What about change logs for model updates? Our ISO wants to see integrity controls around model versions and rollbacks.
[09:46] Marcus: We record model version metadata, the git SHA or artifact hash, rollout timestamps, and can include rollout canary results in evidence.
[09:56] Aisha: Are backups encrypted with same KMS keys?
[10:01] Priya: Yes, backups are encrypted with customer CMKs when you provide them; if Redwood-managed keys are used we'll document key rotation and access controls.
[10:12] Jonathan: Ok let's talk timing: our audit is mid-March, we need artifacts by early March. Can you commit to providing a mapped control set and redacted SOC report by March 3?
[10:22] Liam: We can. Priya, Marcus — is March 3 realistic?
[10:27] Priya: Yes, for redacted SOC 2 and mapping template that's feasible; the signed auditor letter is static we can point them to.
[10:34] Marcus: We'll need your confirmation on KMS choice to include exact policy snippets; if you pick AWS KMS we'll include AWS policy examples.
[10:44] Jonathan: We're leaning AWS KMS to start. We'll confirm by next Wednesday.
[10:50] Renee: One final governance Q: retention of admin accounts and role reviews — do you have evidence of periodic role recertification?
[10:57] Priya: Yes, we have role review logs and periodic access review artifacts; we'll surface a sample quarterly role recert report.
[11:07] Liam: Great. I'll send the Trust Center invite and role recommendations after this call. Priya will upload the redaction template and mapping. Jonathan/Aisha you'll confirm KMS choice and retention numbers. Any other Qs?
[11:20] Jonathan: Not from me. Thanks.
[11:22] Aisha: Nothing else.
[11:24] Renee: Thanks everyone.
[11:26] Liam: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifact links and the KMS integration slot.
[11:31] [end]
questions: Can Redwood provide auditor contact and signed opinion letter?
Does Redwood support customer-managed CMKs and on-prem HSMs?
Can Trust Center roles be mapped to Okta groups?
Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM with 7-year retention?
